bull.b: Royal Caribbean has rebuilt a highly profitable earnings base after the loss-making 2021–2022 period. Sustained revenue expansion, strong operating margins and substantial net income provide internal capacity to fund fleet growth, enhance guest offerings and strengthen competitive positioning.

bull.t: Record Bookings And Raised Earnings Outlook
bull.b: Record booking positions across two future sailing years indicate durable demand visibility rather than reliance only on close-in sales. Raised revenue and earnings guidance, alongside planned capacity and yield growth, supports continued operating momentum over the next several quarters.

The Sandals and Beaches partnership broadens Royal Caribbean beyond ocean cruising into adult-only and family all-inclusive resorts. The expanded platform can increase vacation-wallet reach, enable cross-selling across customer bases and add long-term growth assets in the Caribbean.

bear.b: Although leverage has improved materially from post-pandemic levels, debt remains substantial for a cyclical travel company. High fixed financial obligations can reduce flexibility during weaker demand, increase refinancing sensitivity and constrain the pace of investment or shareholder returns.

Strong operating cash generation is not consistently converting into free cash flow, which remains modest relative to reported earnings and has recently declined sharply. Continued volatility could limit internally funded growth, debt reduction and the company’s ability to absorb major cash uses.

Fuel expense, currency movements and timing-related operating pressures can weigh on margins even when demand remains healthy. These exposures make earnings less predictable, while the planned 2027 first-quarter yield headwind could temporarily reduce the benefit of broader capacity growth.
